title: The Fox and the Grasshopper
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Grasshopper sat chirping in the branches of a tree. A Fox heard her, and, thinking what a dainty morsel she would make, he tried to get her down by a trick. Standing below in full view of her, he praised her song in the most flattering terms, and begged her to descend, saying he would like to make the acquaintance of the owner of so beautiful a voice.

But she was not to be taken in, and replied, "You are very much mistaken, my dear sir, if you imagine I am going to come down: I keep well out of the way of you and your kind ever since the day when I saw numbers of grasshoppers' wings strewn about the entrance to a fox's earth."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what is the Grasshopper doing in the tree?
options: Building a small nest
Hiding from a passing bird
Chirping in the branches
Resting after a long flight

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Fox think when he hears the Grasshopper?
options: That she would make a dainty morsel
That her song was too loud to bear
That she must belong to another fox
That she was warning him of danger

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Fox do to try to get the Grasshopper down?
options: He climbs the tree to reach her directly
He offers her a share of his food
He asks another animal to shake the tree
He praises her song in flattering terms and begs her to descend

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what reason does the Fox give for wanting her to come down?
options: He wants to protect her from a nearby storm
He wants to make the acquaintance of the owner of such a beautiful voice
He wants her to teach him how to sing
He wants to introduce her to his family

questions.prompt: According to the passage, does the Grasshopper fall for the Fox's trick?
options: Yes, she comes down immediately
Yes, but only after some hesitation
No, she was not to be taken in
No, because she never heard him speak

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what had the Grasshopper once seen near a fox's den?
options: Numbers of grasshoppers' wings strewn about the entrance
A pile of bones left from other meals
Other foxes waiting nearby
Tracks leading away from the den

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Grasshopper refuse to come down despite the flattery?
options: She does not understand what the Fox is asking of her
She is too shy to meet new admirers
She is waiting for a better offer from someone else
She has learned from past evidence what foxes actually do to grasshoppers

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the scattered wings at the fox's den prove to the Grasshopper?
options: That the Fox she is speaking to has recently lost a fight
That foxes have eaten other grasshoppers before
That grasshoppers sometimes attack foxes
That the den belongs to a different kind of animal

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "morsel" mean in "a dainty morsel"?
options: A rare and beautiful object
A dangerous kind of trap
A small, tasty bite of food
A short and clever song

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Past evidence of danger should not be ignored, no matter how pleasant the invitation sounds
Grasshoppers should never sing where a fox might hear them
Flattery always works eventually if repeated enough
Foxes are incapable of catching grasshoppers in trees

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where does the Fox stand while speaking to the Grasshopper?
options: Hidden behind the tree
On a branch just above her
Some distance away, out of sight
Below her, in full view

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Grasshopper address the Fox in her reply?
options: "Kind stranger"
"My dear sir"
"Clever fox"
"Old friend"

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Grasshopper say she keeps well out of the way of?
options: Loud noises in the forest
Other grasshoppers nearby
The Fox and his kind
Storms and heavy winds

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Fox choose flattery rather than trying to climb the tree himself?
options: He needs the Grasshopper to come down voluntarily, since he cannot easily reach her in the branches
He believes climbing trees is beneath his dignity
He wants to be introduced properly before eating her
He fears the tree branches are too weak to hold him

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what makes the Grasshopper's refusal especially wise?
options: It is based on a warning she received from another grasshopper
It is based on a general dislike of flattery in any form
It is based on advice given by the tree itself
It is based on direct evidence of what happens to grasshoppers who trust foxes

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the Grasshopper was "not to be taken in"?
options: She was not willing to leave the tree
She was not fooled or deceived
She was not able to hear him clearly
She was not interested in singing further

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Grasshopper is tricked into coming down and is eaten by the Fox
A Fox and a Grasshopper become friends after a long conversation
A Fox tries to lure a Grasshopper down with flattery, but she refuses based on past evidence of danger
A Grasshopper warns other grasshoppers before the Fox can speak
